stories.headline: Want To Apply For Green Card? Return Home First: New US Immigration Rules
stories.summary: The US has introduced new immigration rules requiring aliens in the country temporarily to return to their home country to apply for a Green Card, except in extraordinary circumstances. This change affects foreigners who are in the US on a temporary basis and wish to become lawful permanent residents. The US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) announced the new rule, which applies to individuals seeking permanent residency. Those who want to apply for a Green Card must now do so from their home country, unless they meet specific exceptional criteria. The new rule aims to modify the application process for permanent residency in the US.

stories.headline: Tulsi Gabbard resigns as director of national intelligence, citing husband’s health
stories.summary: Tulsi Gabbard has resigned as Director of National Intelligence, citing her husband Abraham Williams's rare bone cancer diagnosis. Her resignation, effective June 30, was announced in a letter to President Donald Trump, which she posted on social media. Gabbard stated that she needs to step away to be with her husband during this time. Her tenure as Director of National Intelligence was marked by controversy, including dodging questions in a congressional hearing. Gabbard's resignation comes weeks after she faced scrutiny over her responses to congressional inquiries. She will officially leave her position at the end of June to focus on her husband's health and support him during his cancer treatment.

stories.headline: Trump fan Janša wins new term as Slovenia’s prime minister
stories.summary: Slovenia's National Assembly has elected Janez Janša as the country's new prime minister, marking his fourth term in the job. Janša's Slovenian Democratic Party (SDS) formed a coalition with several right-wing parties, securing his path to the top position. The parliamentary vote took place nearly two months after national elections in March, which Janša's party lost. Despite the loss, Janša's candidacy was submitted to Parliament, paving the way for the formation of a new government. Janša has previously served three terms as prime minister, with his last stint ending in 2022. His return to power marks a shift for the small European Union country, with Janša known for his right-wing and nationalist views, similar to those of former US President Donald Trump, whom he has expressed admiration for. The new government is expected to take office under his leadership.

stories.headline: Malian Quran teacher executed by suspected jihadists: sources
stories.summary: Suspected jihadists have executed a Quranic teacher, Salam Abdoul Maiga, in the town of Tonka, northern Mali, for allegedly not practising the right Islam. Maiga was arrested by the jihadists at his school and executed. In a separate incident, a TikTok influencer, Mariam Cisse, was also killed by suspected Al-Qaeda-linked jihadists for allegedly collaborating with the Mali army and filming them. Cisse was shot dead in the street. The executions come amid a joint offensive by pro-independence fighters and jihadists in northern Mali, which has dealt a setback to the military junta in power in Bamako. The junta has been fighting the insurgents with the help of Russian mercenaries. The executions highlight the growing violence and instability in the region. Local and security sources confirmed the incidents, which have raised concerns about the safety of civilians in the area.

stories.headline: Microsoft confirms new Surface laptops with Snapdragon X2 chips are coming later this year
stories.summary: Microsoft has confirmed that new Surface laptops with Snapdragon X2 chips will be available later this year. The company has announced a two-stage rollout, with Intel-based Surface Pro 12 and Laptop 8 models available now for business buyers. The Snapdragon X2-powered versions, targeted at consumers, are expected to launch later in 2026. The delay is reportedly due to component availability issues. Microsoft has not provided a specific release date for the Snapdragon X2-powered Surface devices, but they are expected to feature OLED display upgrades. The new Surface Pro and Laptop models with Intel chips are currently available for business customers, with the Snapdragon X2 versions to follow later this year.

stories.headline: Google is dropping support for almost every Chromecast except this one
stories.summary: Google has dropped support for nearly all Chromecast devices, except for the 2022 Chromecast with Google TV (HD). The company has updated its support page to reflect that most Chromecast devices will no longer receive critical security updates. This change affects several models, including the first-generation Chromecast, which has been experiencing sudden failures. The move has caused stress for owners of older Chromecasts, who will no longer receive essential security updates. The Chromecast with Google TV (HD) remains the only supported device, having been released in 2022. This decision may push users towards alternative streaming services, potentially benefiting Google financially. The change is now reflected on Google's official support page, outlining the new software support policy for its Nest devices, including Chromecast.

stories.headline: Valorant's New Vanguard Update Bricks Cheater's PCs, Riot's Response: "Congrats on your $6k paperweights"
stories.summary: Riot's latest Vanguard update for Valorant is causing cheaters' PCs to malfunction, rendering them unusable. The update is targeting cheating hardware, resulting in affected devices requiring a full operating system reinstall. In response to the issue, Riot tweeted "Congrats on your $6k paperweights," implying that cheaters' expensive hardware is now worthless. The update is part of Riot's efforts to combat cheating in Valorant, and it appears to be effectively disabling cheating devices. Affected users are reporting that their PCs are no longer functional, and Riot's response suggests that the company is taking a firm stance against cheating. The update has been making headlines, with many outlets reporting on the drastic measures being taken to prevent cheating in the game.

stories.headline: Deploying AI Companions in Elder Care: A Privacy Compliance Playbook: Treat AI Companions as High-Risk Programs
stories.summary: Emotionally intelligent AI companions are being deployed in senior living and home care settings to address loneliness and improve engagement. As their use increases, concerns about privacy and compliance have arisen. To address these concerns, AI companions should be treated as high-risk programs, requiring robust safeguards to protect seniors' personal information. Developers and deployers of AI companions must prioritize responsible AI practices, maximizing benefits while minimizing risks. This includes implementing strong privacy measures to prevent potential harm to vulnerable elderly individuals. A privacy compliance playbook is necessary to ensure the safe and responsible deployment of AI companions in elder care, protecting seniors from potential risks and maintaining their trust in these innovative technologies. By doing so, the benefits of AI companions can be fully realized while ensuring the privacy and security of elderly users.

stories.headline: Dominant Mercedes aim to strike a fresh technical blow at Canadian Grand Prix Upgrades for the grid’s leading team will be unveiled in Montreal, where wet weather could also play a part
stories.summary: Mercedes will unveil its first major aerodynamic development package of the year at the Canadian Grand Prix. The upgrades aim to boost the team's performance and potentially end Ferrari's long-held advantage. Despite leading both world championships, team principal Toto Wolff has cautioned that simulation data means nothing until it translates to real track performance. Mercedes is "pretty confident" the upgrades will deliver a performance boost for the W17. The Canadian Grand Prix, taking place on May 22-24, may also be affected by wet weather. The Circuit Gilles-Villeneuve event marks the fifth round of the season, with Mercedes currently atop the drivers' and constructors' standings. Wolff has urged the team to stay balanced as they bring their upgrade package to the Canadian GP. The upgrades will be debuted amidst a disjointed start to the Formula One season.

stories.headline: Makar to remain out for Avalanche in Game 2 of Western Final Defenseman will miss 2nd straight game against Golden Knights with upper-body injury
stories.summary: Colorado Avalanche defenseman Cale Makar will miss Game 2 of the Western Conference final against the Vegas Golden Knights due to an upper-body injury. This will be his second consecutive game missed in the series. Makar participated in skating and shooting drills on Friday morning but was ruled out by coach Jared Bednar. The injury was suffered during the second round of the playoffs. The Golden Knights currently lead the series 1-0 after winning Game 1 with a score of 4-2. Makar's absence will be a significant loss for the Avalanche as they attempt to even the series. The specifics of his injury have not been disclosed, and his status for future games remains uncertain. The Avalanche will face the Golden Knights in Game 2 on Friday night without their star defenseman.

stories.headline: Trevor Story Undergoes Hernia Surgery Boston's shortstop is going to miss a few weeks after undergoing surgery
stories.summary: Boston Red Sox shortstop Trevor Story underwent successful hernia surgery on Thursday. The 33-year-old player is expected to miss several weeks due to the procedure, which was performed in Philadelphia. Story had been placed on the injured list a week prior to the surgery with a sports hernia. The team announced the successful outcome of the operation, but a specific timeline for his return has not been provided. The Red Sox will be without another key player for an extended period, as Story recovers from the surgery. His absence will likely impact the team's lineup and defensive strategy in the coming weeks. The exact duration of his recovery is expected to be a few weeks, although the team has not released a detailed schedule for his return to play.

stories.headline: Michael Carrick's first Man Utd signing announced after appointment Friday delivered some massive transfer news as Man Utd closed in on their first signing of the summer
stories.summary: Manchester United has confirmed the permanent appointment of Michael Carrick as head coach on a two-year contract until 2028, with an option for a further year. Carrick had been in charge since January, replacing Ruben Amorim, and has impressed during his interim spell. Following his appointment, the club is reportedly close to sealing a double transfer worth £140 million, marking their first signings of the summer. This development comes after Carrick's successful stint as interim boss, leading to his permanent appointment. The new head coach will oversee the transfers and the team's preparations for the upcoming season. Carrick's contract extension is a significant move for the club, indicating their confidence in his abilities to lead the team forward. The upcoming transfers are expected to bolster the squad under Carrick's leadership.

stories.headline: India conducts successful test-launch of Agni-1 ballistic missile
stories.summary: India successfully test-fired the Agni-1 ballistic missile from the Integrated Test Range at Chandipur, Odisha, on May 22, 2026. The launch validated key operational and technical parameters under the Strategic Forces Command. This test comes weeks after the successful flight trial of an advanced Agni missile with multiple independently targetable re-entry vehicles off the Odisha coast on May 8. The Agni-1 is a short-range ballistic missile, and the successful test-firing demonstrates India's strategic capabilities and the operational readiness of the Strategic Forces Command. The launch was conducted under the aegis of the Strategic Forces Command, validating all operational and technical parameters. The test-firing of the Agni-1 missile showcases India's ability to develop and deploy advanced missile systems, highlighting its military capabilities.

stories.headline: Ministries ranked on delays, grievance redressal in first-ever performance review
stories.summary: The Indian government has conducted its first-ever performance review of ministries, assessing them on parameters such as delays, grievance redressal, file clearance, and policy inputs. Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan presented the ministry scorecards, ranking them based on their performance. The review aims to evaluate the efficiency and effectiveness of the ministries in addressing citizen grievances and implementing policies. The assessment is part of the government's efforts to improve administrative performance and accountability. The rankings are expected to help identify areas of improvement and enable ministries to take corrective measures to enhance their performance. This initiative marks a significant step towards transparency and accountability in the government's functioning. The performance review is a new approach to evaluating the government's administrative performance.

stories.headline: Centre tells Supreme Court it will bring back persons allegedly ‘pushed’ to Bangladesh
stories.summary: The Centre has informed the Supreme Court that it will bring back individuals allegedly deported to Bangladesh to verify their claims of Indian citizenship. The decision was made due to the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case. A pregnant woman, Sunali Khatun, and her 8-year-old son, who were deported, will be repatriated on humanitarian grounds. The Supreme Court directed the Bengal government to provide medical facilities to Khatun free of cost. The process of bringing back the individuals is expected to take around ten days. The move follows a Calcutta High Court ruling that termed the deportation illegal. The Supreme Court will hear the matter again in July. The Centre's decision aims to verify the citizenship claims of those deported and provide a resolution to the issue. The court's directive ensures humanitarian consideration for those affected.

stories.headline: Twisha Sharma death case: husband taken into custody, M.P. HC allows second autopsy
stories.summary: Samarth Singh, the husband of Twisha Sharma, was taken into custody by the Madhya Pradesh Police after being absconding for days. He is being investigated for dowry death and harassment in connection with Twisha's alleged suicide. The Madhya Pradesh High Court ordered a second autopsy of Twisha Sharma by an AIIMS Delhi team, as requested by her family. Singh had initially filed an anticipatory bail plea but later withdrew it and surrendered. The state government has handed over the probe to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI). Singh currently remains in Bhopal police custody. The developments come after Twisha's family requested a second autopsy, citing concerns over the initial investigation. The CBI will now investigate the case, which has sparked widespread attention and outrage.

stories.headline: US and China Engage in High-Stakes Diplomacy Amid Rising Tensions
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are engaging in high-stakes diplomacy amid rising tensions between the two nations. The talks, held in Beijing, focus on key issues including Taiwan, trade, and regional security. Despite existing tensions over trade, technology, and security, both leaders have stressed cooperation over confrontation. The meetings follow recent discussions between Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng and US officials, where both sides expressed concern over US trade restrictions but committed to collaboration. A rescheduled Trump-Xi meeting in mid-May is expected to lead to a more enduring trade deal, potentially resolving issues before they escalate. Experts believe the negotiations could lead to a significant outcome in 2025, with the US and China seeking to ease tensions and strengthen their fragile relationship. The talks are crucial in shaping the future of US-China relations.

stories.headline: NATO Summit Convenes to Address Global Security Concerns and Geopolitical Shifts
stories.summary: The 2026 NATO Summit is scheduled to take place on July 7-8, 2026, at the Beştepe Presidential Compound in Ankara, Türkiye. NATO Secretary General announced the summit dates on August 19, 2025. Preparations for the event are underway, with Turkish President Erdogan informing former US President Trump that maximum efforts are being made to ensure the summit's success. The summit aims to address global security concerns and geopolitical shifts. US President Biden is expected to attend, and the event will mark a significant gathering of the newly expanded alliance. The summit will provide a platform for member states to discuss key issues and reaffirm their commitment to collective defense. With 32 member states, including 30 in Europe and two in North America, the NATO Summit will be a crucial meeting for addressing global security challenges.

stories.headline: India and Pakistan Agree to Ceasefire Along Disputed Kashmir Border
stories.summary: India and Pakistan have agreed to a ceasefire along the disputed Kashmir border. The agreement comes after a four-day conflict in 2025, which saw India launch a military operation targeting militant camps in Pakistan and Pakistan-administered Kashmir. Pakistan retaliated with drone incursions and shelling along the Line of Control. Despite the ceasefire, tensions remain high, with both countries maintaining hardline stances. The conflict is the latest in a long-standing dispute over the Kashmir region, which has been a point of contention between India and Pakistan since the India-Pakistan War of 1971. Pakistan's foreign ministry has confirmed that the ceasefire understanding with India remains intact, and Islamabad is committed to holding the agreement. The region remains volatile, with recent terrorist attacks in Kashmir highlighting the ongoing tensions between the two nations. The ceasefire agreement aims to reduce cross-border violence.

stories.headline: Russian President Announces Major Foreign Policy Overhaul in Response to International Pressure
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin has announced a major overhaul of the country's foreign policy in response to international pressure. The move comes as Putin faces domestic pressure with the Ukraine war entering its fifth year. Recently, Putin met with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing, where Xi described the bilateral relationship as "precious" in the current international context. Xi emphasized the need for China and Russia to strengthen and defend their shared interests. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov also visited Beijing in April, meeting with Xi to discuss the importance of their alliance. The overhaul is expected to prioritize a "sovereign foreign policy," with Russia seeking to assert its independence and protect its interests on the global stage. Putin's visit to Beijing contrasts with a recent trip by former US President Trump, highlighting Russia's shifting diplomatic priorities.

stories.headline: Indian Equities Rally: Banks Lead as Global Trends Boost Market Sentiment
stories.summary: Indian equity markets rebounded strongly, driven by global investor sentiment and hopes of a rate cut. The BSE Sensex posted its biggest single-day gain since November 29, closing at a three-month high. Banking stocks led the gains, while the India VIX dropped 5%, indicating lower volatility. Global trends, including a 2.3% rise in Brent crude to $104.7 per barrel, also boosted market sentiment. Easing geopolitical tensions and a decline in crude oil prices contributed to the rebound. The rally was a sharp turnaround, supported by improved global risk sentiment. The benchmark indices closed at a three-month high, with banking stocks driving the gains. The market's positive movement was also influenced by global market trends, including cautious sentiment due to rising US bond yields.

stories.headline: Stock market today: Sensex gains 230 points, Nifty 50 ends above 23,700; banking stocks shine
stories.summary: The Sensex gained 230 points, ending at 75,415.35, while the Nifty 50 closed above 23,700. Banking stocks performed well, contributing to the market's positive trend. The Sensex rose by 0.31% with a 232-point increase. The Nifty 50 surpassed the 23,700 mark, driven by the strong performance of banking sector stocks. This uptrend is a notable development in the Indian equity markets, which had previously experienced a weak day with Nifty nearing the 24,000 mark and Nifty Bank facing a decline. The current gain indicates a shift in market sentiment, with banking stocks leading the way.

stories.headline: Nifty 50, Sensex Extend Gains To Hit Fresh Day's High, Financials Lead Rally
stories.summary: The BSE Sensex and Nifty 50 extended gains to hit fresh highs in afternoon trade on Friday, May 22. The Sensex rose 514.96 points to 75,698.32, touching an intraday high of 75,810.97, while the Nifty 50 increased 147.70 points to 23,802.40, hitting a high of 23,835.65. The Indian Rupee recovered to Rs 95 per US dollar mark earlier in the session, contributing to the positive cues. The rally was led by financials, with the market responding to several positive cues, including stronger US-Iran peace negotiations. The benchmark indices ended the previous day higher, with the Nifty 50 closing at 23,719.30 and the Sensex at 75,415.35, marking a marginal increase for the week.

stories.headline: No fourth headline available
stories.summary: No fourth federal stimulus check has been authorized by Congress or announced by the IRS as of May 2025. Despite this, rumors and misinformation continue to circulate online, with misleading headlines and scam messages suggesting additional stimulus payments are forthcoming. These false claims have been spread through social media and online news outlets, causing confusion among the public. Official sources, including the IRS and Congress, have not confirmed any plans for a fourth stimulus check. The lack of credible information has led to a proliferation of scams and misinformation, highlighting the need for reliable sources and fact-checking in staying informed about national news and developments.

stories.headline: United flight rerouted after passenger tries to open door at 36,000 feet
stories.summary: A United Airlines flight from Newark to Guatemala City was diverted to Washington Dulles International Airport after a passenger allegedly tried to open a rear cabin door at 36,000 feet. The incident occurred on a 737 MAX aircraft, which was forced to make an emergency landing due to the unruly passenger's behavior. According to air traffic control, the passenger also assaulted another traveler. Although the door could not be opened at cruising altitude, the incident was serious enough to warrant a diversion. The flight, which originated from Newark Liberty Airport, was bound for Guatemala City when the disturbance occurred, prompting the pilot to alter course and land at Washington Dulles. The Federal Aviation Administration is aware of the incident, which highlights the risks of unruly passenger behavior on commercial flights.

stories.headline: AI cracks 80-year-old mathematics challenge - researchers are astonished
stories.summary: Mathematicians at OpenAI have cracked an 80-year-old geometry challenge using a single prompt from an AI chatbot. The problem, known as the "unit distance" conjecture, has been solved autonomously by a new general-purpose reasoning model. This marks the first time AI has solved a prominent open problem in mathematics without human intervention. The solution is considered significant enough to be published in a top mathematics journal if it had been achieved by humans. OpenAI's achievement is a major milestone for AI reasoning and scientific research, demonstrating the potential of AI to autonomously solve complex mathematical problems. The breakthrough has astonished researchers, including those familiar with the work of mathematician Paul Erdős, who published related research. The solution is a notable example of AI's growing capabilities in scientific research.

stories.headline: Gilead Sciences, Inc. today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted accelerated approval for Hepcludex® (bulevi...
stories.summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted accelerated approval for Hepcludex (bulevirtide-gmod) injection to treat chronic hepatitis delta virus (HDV) infection in adults without cirrhosis. Gilead Sciences, Inc. announced the approval, marking the first treatment for HDV in the United States. Hepcludex is administered via injection and has been approved for adults with HDV infection without advanced liver disease. The FDA's accelerated approval allows for earlier approval of drugs that treat serious conditions and fill an unmet medical need. Hepcludex's approval is based on its efficacy in treating HDV infection, providing a new treatment option for patients with this rare and deadly liver infection. The drug is expected to provide a significant benefit to patients with limited treatment options.

stories.headline: Lumentum Holdings Inc.’s Q3 FY2026 surge: $808M revenue (+90% YoY), 200G EML boom, margin expansion, and AI demand tailwinds.
stories.summary: Lumentum Holdings Inc.'s Q3 FY2026 revenue surged to $808.4 million, a 90% year-over-year increase. The company reported GAAP EPS of $1.50 and non-GAAP EPS of $2.37. The revenue growth was driven by a boom in 200G EML sales and tailwinds from artificial intelligence demand. Lumentum's non-GAAP operating margin expanded by over 2,100 basis points. For Q4, the company guided revenue to range from $960 million to $1.01 billion, with a midpoint of $980 million, exceeding the estimated $936 million. The strong performance and positive outlook indicate a significant increase in demand for Lumentum's products, particularly in the 200G EML segment, driven by the growing need for high-speed data transmission and AI applications.
